submission.justification:
Algorithm-L1 with a threshold of 39 GeV achieves the highest signal efficiency of 92.837% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. Through systematic simulation testing across all three candidate algorithms and various thresholds within the allowed 20-60 GeV range, Algorithm-L1 consistently outperformed the alternatives:

- Algorithm-L1 at 39 GeV: 92.837% efficiency (recommended)
- Algorithm-L3 at optimal threshold (30 GeV): 84.716% efficiency
- Algorithm-L2 at optimal threshold (40 GeV): 75.027% efficiency

Algorithm-L1 provides approximately 8 percentage points higher efficiency than Algorithm-L3 and 18 percentage points higher than Algorithm-L2. The iterative topological clustering with learned calibration approach (Algorithm-L1) is superior for this signature, and the optimal threshold of 39 GeV balances signal acceptance against background rejection to maximize efficiency at the allocated rate.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 at 39 GeV achieves 92.837% signal efficiency, which is the highest efficiency found across all tested algorithms and thresholds at the 8 kHz allocated rate.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate algorithms: 'Algorithm-L1: iterative topological clustering with a learned calibration.'

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware
requirements.evidence: All three candidate algorithms, including Algorithm-L1, 'fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs)' as stated in the specifications.
The recommended threshold of 39 GeV falls within the required range of 20-60 GeV.
